subject: bat
readings: head at +y (up) in the ZY panel -> ZY panel is the profile, XY panel is the FRONT (spread-wing) view, as in the worked bat example
XY panel: left wingtip (23,6), right wingtip (1,7), shoulder/chest (9,7), body center (9,10)
ZY panel: torso top (8,2)-(10,8), tail base (8,14/16), tail tip (8,24) -> long whip tail, length ~10 in y
XZ panel: head (8,8), folded wing mass (1-8,13-16), extended wing/finger reaching (24,12-14) confirming wings run along x, depth z~8-9 for trunk
Wings read as asymmetric in this pose (23 vs 1 from chest) but per proportion rule both wings are authored with equal length, taken from the more extended (left) wing reading
notes: Head counts as a leaf since it forms a distinct lobe with ears above the chest. Wings and legs were each split into two segments (shoulder->elbow->wingtip, hip->knee->foot); these joints are anatomical inference, not directly marked on the grid, chosen as midpoints with the slight droop/upsweep visible in the XY silhouette. The tail is authored as a single flap (abdomen->tip) since no intermediate joint is visible; its length (~10) is read from the ZY panel where it hangs furthest (to y=24), which is more complete than its truncated appearance in the XY panel. Depth (z) values were kept nearly constant (~9) for trunk-mounted limbs since the XZ panel shows most of the body sitting in a narrow z-band, except the wing finger which sweeps out in x per the XZ panel, matching the XY wingspan. Left/right assigned assuming the XY panel is a front view facing the viewer (animal's left = image right, +x).
